summary: San Bernardino National Forest lookout about 12 miles east of Big Bear; a 1943 newspaper item is the only detailed source, and FFLA lists it as gone.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; no source gives a removal date or describes the site now

events.note: Lookout Raymond W. Smith living at the station in April 1943
Rattlesnake bite while clearing debris near the station (newspaper dated April 27, 1943); anti-venom given at the station

evidence.supports: Station on Tip Top Mountain in the San Bernardino National Forest at 8,500 feet
evidence.quote: Tip Top mountain, where the lookout station is located, is at an elevation of 8,500 feet.

evidence.supports: Tip Top Mountain is in the San Bernardino National Forest
Raymond W. Smith, a San Bernardino National Forest lookout, bitten by a rattlesnake (article dated April 27, 1943)
evidence.quote: Bitten on the hand by a three-foot timber rattlesnake, Raymond W. Smith, 30, San Bernardino National forest lookout

evidence.supports: Bitten while clearing debris near the station, which is 12 miles east of Big Bear
evidence.quote: Mr. Smith was bitten on the back of the hand as he cleaned up a pile of debris near his lookout station on Tip Top mountain, located 12 miles east of Big Bear
Rushing to the lookout station, where he lives

evidence.supports: Radio message sent to the Big Bear ranger station
evidence.quote: a radio message was sent to the Big Bear ranger station

evidence.supports: Ranger called a doctor, who went to the station
evidence.quote: Ranger Wayne Allen called Dr. Moyer of Big Bear, who immediately left for Tip Top mountain

evidence.supports: Doctor gave anti-venom at the lookout station
evidence.quote: Dr. Moyer administered anti-venom treatment to Mr. Smith at the lookout station

evidence.supports: Smith gave himself first aid before the anti-venom treatment
evidence.quote: Mr. Smith, who gave himself first aid and then took anti-venom treatment from the physician

evidence.supports: Smith taken back to Big Bear for observation
evidence.quote: then brought him back to Big Bear where he will remain for observation for at least 24 hours

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Tip Top Mountain in San Bernardino County as gone
evidence.quote: Tip Top Mountain San Bernardino 34.25170 -116.69150 Unknown Gone

notes_for_editor: Only one detailed source: a 1943 San Bernardino County Sun item transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page (original not checked). Built date, design and removal are not in any source read. Tip Top is not in the cached firetower.org former-site list for California (matched on the name). Do not present the 1943 staffing as current. Check San Bernardino National Forest records before publishing anything about the site. An earlier draft named a site author; the cached page text does not name one, so the source no longer does.
